source_en: Returning home after closing the corner grocery store.
Shop sold out by noon. Closed up. Going home.
Dropping off the daily register keys at the manager's.
Opened the empty shop again. Nobody came. Going home.
Checking if the industrial freezers still have power.
Stood in the bread line. Nothing. Going home anyway.
Locked the shop. Windows are gone. Going home.
Going home to sit in my room. Shift's over.
Fulfilling mandatory residency census requirements.
Going home to my wife and kids. Big family dinner tonight.
Collecting my pension. Retired from the shop last year.
Hosting a party tonight for the whole block. Can't wait!
Unloading a fresh delivery at the shop. Shelves are full.
Visiting my neighbour. He invited me over for dinner.
Volunteering at the triage centre. I love helping out.
Opening the shop early. Big sale tomorrow, very busy.
Visiting. I don't live here, I'm on a business trip.
Back from the dance hall. Best night of my life.
Here’s my ID and the form. I filled them out while waiting for bread.
I’m just going home. The shop ran out of everything by noon anyway.
Is your stamp working? Everything else in this city seems to be broken.
People were fighting over batteries today. I just watched. It was like a movie.
The lights in the shop keep flickering. It’s hard to see the prices.
Here’s the paper. I don't really care if it's right or not. You decide.
I locked the front door, but the windows are already gone. Doesn't matter.
I’m going to go sit in my room until the sky finishes turning gray.
My shift is over. I think the whole world’s shift is over.
Cool. Have a fun time in your little box, officer.
Right. I’m going to go stare at a wall now.
Whatever. See you when the lights go out for good.
A holding cell? Does it have a bed? I could use a nap.
Fine. At least I don't have to tell people we're out of sugar in there.
Put me wherever. It’s all the same to me at this point.
Oh. I guess... I don't have to... go to work... tomorrow...
This is... a very... loud way... to end a shift...
Finally... I can... stop... waiting... in lines.
Okay.
Does it have a chair? Great. Fine.
Sure. Lock me up. I’ll add it to the list of things that don’t matter.
Hm. Didn’t even need to think about it, did you.
Right. Okay. That’s… fine too… I guess…
At least I don’t… have to face another line… tomorrow…
Where are you coming from?
The shop. Sold out by noon. I stood in the bread line anyway, then closed up.
The shop. Checked if the freezers still have power. They don't. You can smell it.
The shop, I think. I locked the door. The windows are already gone. Doesn't matter.
The shop on the western block. Been working there a few months now.
Home. My wife made dinner, so I left the shop early.
The train station. I only moved to this district last year.
Are you experiencing any symptoms?
No. Tired. I'm always tired. That's not new.
I stopped feeling cold about a week ago. Not sure if that counts.
Everything aches a little. Sleep doesn't fix it. Nothing fixes anything.
Never tired. I sleep ten hours a night and the shop is always full. I love it.
I'm freezing all the time, officer. Can't get warm no matter what I do.
Nothing aches. My neighbour and I played cards all night. He says I look well.
Is your stamp working? Ours at the shop broke twice this week.
There was no bread again. I stood in line for an hour anyway. Force of habit.
You look like you are about to ask me something. Please do not.
Take your time. I have nothing urgent waiting for me on the other side.
The shop is empty. I still open it every morning. I am not sure why.
Are you cold? I stopped feeling cold about a week ago. Not sure what that means.
Someone was crying in the street on the way here. I walked past. There was nothing to do.
Does any of this feel pointless to you? Just curious. I will not be offended.
I keep coming through here. Pure habit at this point. Take your time.
I have nowhere to be. Neither does anyone.
